utterances.text: Tell me, were all dilemmas resolved in terms of the certificates on having completed a particular grade or year? Was it not possible on that basis to continue regular schooling in the school system of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If we do not take into account technical constraints or, rather, objective constraints in terms of capacity, can we not conclude that in the school year of 1993-1994 -- or, rather, let me phrase it in a positive manner. In the school year of 1993-1994, the regular schooling system of the Republic of Croatia, did it include refugees who were Bosniaks, the children of Bosniak refugees?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me -- elementary schools, secondary schools, extraterritorial, there were three of them. Tell me, children of Bosniaks continued their schooling in secondary schools according to the available capacity of these schools. Can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On secondary schools?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Secondary schools.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned three extraterritorial schools. Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to your own information and data, you said that there were three extraterritorial secondary schools.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And not all refugee children, Bosniaks, could attend these schools. Now I'm asking you whether the children of Bosniak refugees continued their education in regular secondary schools of the Republic of Croatia in accordance with the available capacities of the existing schools.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Krajsek, I'm not going to ask you any more questions about schools, but if we have enough time, perhaps we could clarify your visit to the Croat refugees in Pinete, because it seems to me that due to a variety of circumstances there was some confusion there. Can you tell us how many times you came to Pinete?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twice, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us precisely what time of year it was? Was it very hot? Was it in summer or was it late autumn or ...

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time, it could have been the summer, because I practically went to all the locations that I knew of at that time, because we had just legalised extraterritorial schools. It could have been the summer period. My second visit, the one that I mentioned due to my visit to the Croat refugees, was perhaps in the autumn. However, there's no need for me to try to remember. There is an exact date on my report as to when it was that I visited.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm not going to ask you anything else about that. Perhaps we could also go back to the documents of that summer, after the stadium of Poljud. That's where the refugees from the Lasva River valley were. But what I'm interested in is whether you had any information or, rather, did you know -- did you talk to the citizens of Vares who, in the beginning of November, fled from Vares?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, Ms. Krajsek, now I'm going to ask you something that all my colleagues asked you, the ones who asked you before me, but I'm going to phrase if in a different way. Do you know of any other country that did more for refugees from Bosnia-Herzegovina than Croatia did?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are putting an unpleasant question to me because, as far as I'm concerned, Croatia and other countries did a great deal indeed for refugees from BH.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I want you to answer my question, whether a single country did more than the Republic of Croatia did.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are our yardsticks? I do not know how to answer that question. I appreciate the enormous effort, and I appreciate that. It was enormous, this assistance, but I really cannot make any evaluations in terms of more or less, enough, whatever.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If you yourself cannot assess that, I'm not going to insist on that any further. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have used up my time, and I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. We will now have a 20-minute break, and we will resume 20 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, madam.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam, hopefully just a few questions to see if I can give you the opportunity to clarify a few things, perhaps, that came up during cross-examination. Is it correct, madam, we can probably well understand that you were quite busy during this time taking care of the refugees from Bosnia-Herzegovina that were in Croatia itself.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My working day lasted on an average between 12 to 17 hours over a 24-hour period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: On the question of the location of your offices - you may have made a passing reference to this; if you did, I'm not sure it was clear - were your offices also located in the same building as the embassy itself?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had an office for a very brief period of time in the basement of the embassy building, and two or three months later, or maybe even before that, I relocated to a completely different address.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So can the Judges understand, in reference to some of the questions that have been put to you about what you knew or didn't know at the embassy, you arrived at the embassy, I believe you said, on the 1st of March, approximately, the 1st of March, 1993, and you were only actually in the embassy for approximately two or three months.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can ask you to -- you still have all the binders there. We may have overwhelmed you with paper, probably. If you can find in the Prosecution bundle that we worked looked at, worked with, on Monday and Tuesday morning. If I can ask you to go to Exhibit 3708. In light of the questions that have been asked about the visit to the Bosnian Croat refugees from Central Bosnia or Lasva Valley, if you can look just a bit more carefully at Mr. Rebic's letter. Tell me when you have that, please.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can go to the -- I believe it would be the end of the third paragraph. That third paragraph starts with the word "Second," and then it goes on toward the end, and that's when Mr. Rebic expressed his concern or his surprise, saying that Ms. Turkovic had not shown any interest in the displaced Croats from Lasva Valley. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see that portion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, according to Mr. Rebic's letter, he says -- at the very end of that he says, "...who were expelled by Muslims from their homes and which we have had to accept about a month ago." So if Mr. Rebic's letter is dated the 26th of July, 1993, which it is, then if Mr. Rebic is correct, then we're talking about -- these are people who arrived sometime in late -- approximately late June 1993. Is that --

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then if you'll go to the exhibit that -- Ms. Turkovic's letter, which should be the next document, 3765. Maybe I missed -- yes, 3765.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This is the letter that you've looked at now in the last several days a couple of times at least. Towards the next -- well, in the paragraph that starts with the words "Mr. Rebic." Again, we come back to the language where Ms. Turkovic says: "With regard to that, I would like to stress that immediately after the arrival of refugees from the Central Bosnia, I went to Poljud to visit them. I issued orders to secure supplies," et cetera. Now, in light of everything that's been said, madam, I mean, do you stand by this statement? And, to your knowledge, is it true that Ms. Turkovic visited those displaced persons in approximately -- sometime in July 1993? Or perhaps even the end of June?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat her answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, you've been asked to give your answer again. Apparently there was some problem with the interpreters hearing it.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by the statement when I said that I know that Mrs. Turkovic visited the refugees at the Poljud stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, again, on the same general topic, if you can go to Exhibit 4150. 4150.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you could turn almost to the end of the document, it's the next-to-last paragraph, the paragraph that we've again looked at before starting with the words "About the refugees of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina ..." Do you see it? Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Karnavas asked you if, in fact, it wasn't a bit inconsistent for you to say in the letter here that you had no information at all in contrast, for example, to then your evidence that, as one example, Ms. Turkovic had gone to visit the displaced Croats from the Lasva Valley. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise, but could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, of course. If you have that question -- if you have the information there -- and actually let me come at it a bit differently. You say: "About the refugees of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina - Croats - sadly, we have no information at all as we do not receive the information about them, nor do we receive any other information from the Office of Displaced" -- probably a missing word, "Persons and Refugees, and they themselves are not contacting the embassy." Let me pause on those two items before I come back to the question I first put to you. When you say you do not receive information, are you saying here -- who are you referring to, if anyone, when you say you do not receive information? From whom?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I write exactly that I'm not receiving information from the Office for Refugees and Displaced Persons of the Republic of Croatia. What I'm also saying and writing is that the Croat refugees from BH are not contacting the embassy or, rather, the office for refugees. So those are the sources that I quote when referring to the fact that I did not receive information from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Madam, I think I need to clarify your answer, because at least what was translated or came into the transcript, you said, "I don't think I write exactly that I'm not receiving ..." It's a bit of a double-negative or at least a bit awkward. When you say "I am not" -- there's two parts -- let me suggest to you there's two parts to the sentence. One is they themselves are not contacting the embassy. Now, when you say "they themselves are not contacting the embassy," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the refugees. And when I refer to the Office for Refugees and Displaced Persons of the Republic of Croatia, then I mean that despite the questions about information related to people who came from BH, I still did not receive information or responses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, coming back to my original question. In light of what you told us about, for example, Ms. Turkovic going to visit the displaced Croats from Central Bosnia, and you've told us about going to see the displaced Croats from Kakanj, the Vares-Kakanj area, would you agree that perhaps in reference to the statement "We have no information," that perhaps would be a bit of an overstatement to say you had no information?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would be exaggerated along those lines, because we had information but from other sources; first of all, from the parents of the children of refugees who were organised in extraterritorial schools and, of course, through the information media, public information media, of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me refer you to the working group that you were a part of with Mr. Zubak and Mr. Tadic, if we can come back to that and some questions that arose in that area. I think there's no disagreement that the Tudjman-Izetbegovic agreement was signed on the 14th of September, 1993, which we looked at, and in fact we saw that in the presidential transcript from the next day, the 15th, that you were appointed -- your name was actually in the transcript as having been appointed to one of the working groups; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'd like you, if you can find, or if it's not there, in the bundle of the Prlic -- Jadranko Prlic exhibits, 1D, if you have it there or if the usher can assist us, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Apparently the usher doesn't have a bundle now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What's the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: 1D 190-1590. Perhaps while that's being done, for the rest of the court, it could also be put up on e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam, I'd just like for you to scan through the document for a moment. I'm not going to ask you detailed questions about the document, but I'd like you to have some sense of the document, if you could look at it, please.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have leafed through the document quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, in looking at this document, whether this was the first -- reflects a record, if you will, of the first meeting of the working group on the 25th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fully, because I can see my signature and the fact that I initialled the rest of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, in that regard, then, we see that among the other persons at the meeting, of course, were Mr. Zubak and Mr. Tadic, and I think you were already asked by Mr. Karnavas if all four of you didn't, in fact, sign the record, which I think was clear. Had you ever met or had any communications, conversations, with Mr. Tadic prior to the meeting on the 25th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On condition that this was, indeed, the first meeting. I think it was. At the official meeting held for the first time, I informed Mr. -- I met Mr. Tadic for the first time and had meetings with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And let me ask you this before moving forward: You were asked questions about whether you considered that you represented "the Muslim nation," and I think we have your answer, but did you consider -- just by way of clarification and as a further foundation for the next couple of questions, did you believe that you were participating in this working group as a representative of only Muslims?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this working group I worked by appointment at the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, working in the name of all the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And with reference to this working group that was set up following the agreement on the 14th of September, 1993, between President Tudjman of Croatia and President Izetbegovic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you ever have any information or understanding why President -- did you ever have any understanding why President Tudjman's appointed representatives were both senior officials of Herceg-Bosna and not officials of the Croatian government?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know at the time that they were senior officials of the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When did you learn that, if you did?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was only upon returning to the country. I didn't know that at this period. That's certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, in going back to Mr. Tadic, then, you told us during direct examination that you then had a number of conversations with Mr. Tadic about moving the Croats from the Kakanj -- excuse me, the Kakanj-Vares area out of that location. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise, but could you repeat that. I've lost the train of thought. I wasn't able to hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry. It's probably my mistake, and I know it's been a long week. You testified -- I just want to confirm you recall testifying on direct examination that you had a number of conversations with Mr. Tadic after first meeting him in which he initiated the subject of relocating the Bosnian Croats from the Kakanj-Vares area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And was it -- can you confirm to the Judges, was it sometime after those conversations that in fact this group of Croats from the Kakanj-Vares area were then moved to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise, and to Mr. Scott, too, but I think we should clarify the following: The concept of Croats from the Kakanj-Vares area is highly imprecise. I think it would be important for us to know whether we're dealing with people from Kakanj who were temporarily put up in Vares and that that is why a solution was found for these people of Kakanj from Vares. So that's one topic which we dealt with during the period discussed by the witness. And the citizens of Vares who, at the beginning of November, left Vares is quite a different topic. So could we clarify what we mean? I think it will be especially important and beneficial to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: As to who, Your Honour, from the Kakanj-Vares area, we've talked about this for some days, not only with this witness but with a number other witnesses. I suggest there should be no question about that for now. As to the timing, whether this is the October -- a group from October or a group from November, again, I leave it to the rest of the evidence. If we're referring to those who arrived, and there seems to be no question about this, that they arrived in the Pinete area at the end of October, then obviously we're not talking about the ones from November.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam, my question to you was, concerning the Bosnian Croat persons who as a result of various events had found themselves by October in the area of Vares, and after your conversations with Mr. Tadic, was it after that time that you then visited -- after these conversations with Mr. Tadic that you visited the Croats, displaced persons, after they arrived in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you clarify your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. I don't know what the problem with translation is at the moment, but I'll try to say it again. Madam, you've told us in the last few minutes, you've clarified when you first met Mr. Tadic, looked at the minutes of the meeting, you've also confirmed that it was after conversations with Mr. Tadic that -- when he raised this topic. My only question to you now: So was it after these conversation with Mr. Tadic about moving the Bosnian Croats from the Vares area, was it after that that you then went and visited these Croats after they arrived in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely it. After the discussion at these meetings, I went to Pinete and visited the Croats who arrived in Croatia from the area of Kakanj and Vares, and some other places, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can I ask you to look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could have in e-court, please, in the interests of time, could I -- because I don't believe it's in the original bundle, but can you please pull up Exhibit P 05996. Actually, either way. It is in the bundle. I'm sorry. I missed it.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: With reference to the second -- well, the first actual paragraph after the introduction, if you will: "On the 20th of October, 1993, approximately 5.500 Croats expelled from the municipalities of Kakanj and Zenica arrived to the municipality of Vares. Muslim armed forces expelled them from their centuries-old hearth," according to this letter. "A reception point was organised for these displaced persons in the Capljina municipality." Then it goes on. If I can then ask you to go to the second page. It may be different in the Bosnian version, so I'm not sure. If you go on down, there are some numbers. And for the area of Novi Grad, do you see the number 1.520 on the 20th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to assist the Prosecutor as well linked to this group. I think that the title of the document is highly precise and tells us where the group is from. It says, "Report on the expelled Croats from the municipalities of Kakanj in Zenica who arrived from the Vares municipality," which means that this doesn't deal with refugees from Vares. This document clearly points out that it is from Kakanj and Zenica, those who were temporarily in Vares. So this is quite clear on the basis of this document. And I think this is very important, it's an important point, because the witness, both in her written statement and in oral testimony, she said that they were refugees from Vares on several occasions, whereas the document that the Prosecutor is referring to now and the document that he referred to yesterday, which is P 05960, clearly show that they are expelled persons from Kakanj and Zenica. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that's the only -- if that's the nature of the dispute, which I perhaps have not comprehended, that that was specifically the nature of any dispute about this evidence, I don't think there is a dispute. I think everyone -- but I also think the Chamber has heard evidence about how other Croats from Kakanj came and were in the Vares area and has heard other evidence about how they were then -- Croats from that area were then moved out. As to the witness's testimony, just so there's no confusion or mischaracterisation about that, in paragraph 110 of her statement - in the interests of time, Your Honour, I'm not going to ask her; everyone has the statement - it says, "Eventually Bosnian Croats from Kakanj and Vares left and ended up in Istria." But if there's no further dispute about that, I thought the question was about the date and not about whether they came also from Kakanj. But I think that covers the topic in any event.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you, please, about the access and freedom of movement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want to say, before the Prosecutor moves on to another area, that I referred to this point yesterday because the witness, in paragraph 110 of her statement and that is under 92 ter, she says that the Croats arrived from both Kakanj and Vares, and quite obviously, according to the documents shown by the Prosecutor, they were from Kakanj and Zenica, not Kakanj and Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to waste my time belabouring the issue further. The totality of this evidence, including this evidence and other evidence, is before the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam, I want to move on to another topic because we only have a few minutes, and that is the question of freedom of movement of the Muslim displaced persons that found themselves in Croatia in the second half of 1993, and maybe it helps us. I'm focusing now on those who came roughly in the time period between the latter part of July, when the Mostar group arrived, and later the Ljubuski group in August, and the prisoners from Dretelj in September, October. That's the time period I'm talking about. Could you just clarify, because I'm not -- to be perfectly honest, I'm not sure what the balance of your evidence is about that. Did those Muslim displaced persons have freedom of movement to move around Croatia at will?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: These displaced persons had no freedom of movement around Croatia. I might have said that the refugees had the right to free movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you, if you still have it -- sorry. In the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Again, if the usher could assist us. If we could look into the Praljak bundle, I believe at 3D 01036.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really don't want to take up my colleague's time, but do please take a look at the previous answer given by the witness on page 105, line 1 -- lines 1 to 3. Just two sentences, two completely contradictory sentences. Now, how are we going to draw our arguments from that when the time comes? So would the Prosecutor be good enough to clear this up. The refugees could have had freedom of movement or not had freedom of movement, to the best of the witness's knowledge. I know what she's talking about, I know what she means, but I don't want to be faced in a situation where, in the final brief, I spend three pages writing about what this statement by the witness now might or might not mean and imply.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's exactly why I asked the question. To be perfectly transparent, that's exactly the reason I asked the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam, you've also heard the comments of counsel. So in light of what's been said - I assume that's been interpreted to you or you have heard it in a language you understand - there does seem to be a suggestion of some inconsistency in what you've said. So can you clarify: What was the freedom of movement of these persons who arrived in Croatia in the second half of 1993?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The persons who arrived at that time did not have a recognised status of refugee in the Republic of Croatia, so they were not able to move around. And questions linked to the Mostar and Ljubuski and Dretelj group, I always claimed, and still maintain, that they had no freedom of movement in the Republic of Croatia. When I was asked questions about freedom of movement referring to refugees, that is to say, BH citizens with a recognised refugee status in the Republic of Croatia, my answer was then, as it is now, that to the best of my knowledge they did have the right to freedom of movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam, again, time is short, and in reference to -- I don't know if we have, really, time to find the particular items because it's quite -- some of these documents are quite long. Mr. Praljak showed you a number of documents and tables again with, I guess, Croatian dinars, I suppose it would be, money spent by the Croatian government on education. I thought it was in 3D 01036.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Perhaps my colleague can assist me while I go on to another topic. I can't find it at the moment, I have to admit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: While she's doing that, if we can go back to the Prlic bundle please, 1D 01329. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you could go to -- I'm just going to the third page of this document which lists -- starting with the date, the 15th of June, 1993, and then goes on to list the number of convoys down through -- well, at the bottom of that page, 6th of July, and then it continues on over. But according to this document, the title, at least as translated, is "Passages Approved for the Following Convoys from 1 June 1993 to 10 December 1993," and my question to you is actually quite -- I think, I hope, quite straightforward. In looking at those lists, do you have any personal knowledge that any of those convoys actually travelled or reached their intended destination during that time? And if it helps to be more specific, if you find for the 24th of June, on the 24th of June -- well, there's actually a number going to Zenica. I think you'll find that on the same page you were looking at a moment ago. Do you have any personal knowledge that any of those convoys actually reached their intended destination?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in Zenica at the time, but all the information that reached me in Croatia that had to do with convoys and the delivery of humanitarian aid in Bosnia-Herzegovina was the same. It was always said that not a single convoy reached its ultimate destination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And one further example because it relates to, in particular, Mostar, if I can find it again. On the second page, if you go down to the locations in the column marked for location or destination, odrediste, forgive me if I mispronounce it, but if you look down in that and find the first one for -- there's an entry for Mostar, 3rd of July, 1993. Do you have any --

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether that convoy in fact reached and entered Mostar around that time, July 1993?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can ask you to go to -- in the bundle of the exhibits for the Stojic Defence, 2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And again I may need the assistance of the usher please, 2D 00498. I have my work copy. I'm sorry. I would have thought that the registry still had them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, if you have that, 2D 00498. And then if I can ask you to turn into the document until you find the page -- the English page I'm going to refer to, Your Honours, for those working in English, on the top of the page, top right corner of the page -- not the very top number, but it has what we call the ERN number, 03284603. And the English version -- on the bottom of the page, it has 2D 38-0213, and in the Bosnian or Croatian language version, it is on -- on the bottom of the page, it has 2D 38-0196. So hopefully if you can find either the English or -- that will assist you, or find the original language version. Do you have the one on the bottom that's marked 2D 38-0196? Those ones are in numerical order, if you find those.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it on the monitor now, what I'm looking for?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's look. Yes. Correct. I believe it is. Yes.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll look at the monitor then, because I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My thanks to the usher for that assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam, on that document if we could just very quickly look -- just so there's no misunderstanding on some of these numbers, if you can assist us, or perhaps there won't be any disagreement about it. In fact, it's written on the -- in item number 4, 12.000 -- there's HDR, again, I hope there will be no misunderstanding -- "HRD" stands for Croatian dinar; do you know that, madam?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see this, but I don't know what these amounts refer to. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you look at Valuta in the middle column, it gives the reference. And my first question to you, as one of my colleagues says step by step --

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "HRD," is that Croatian dinar?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And it indicates in the next column to the right, 12.000. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you see that apparently above that someone has written in "1 Deutschmark equals 560 HRD"?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just so the Chamber is aware of what that number actually means, do you then understand that 12.000 Croatian dinars in June 1993 was about 8 Deutschmarks? Does that sound about right to you? If I have to do the math, we can do it, but that's what I've been told. I hope my sources are correct. Do you understand, madam? Do you have any recollection that as of June 1993, 1 Deutschmark equalled about 1.500 Croatian dinar? If you don't, madam, in the interests of time, I'm sure we can establish that.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that that is not correct. I think it was between 360 to 400 Croatian dinars, one German mark, that is. To the best of my recollection, one German mark -- or, rather, a hundred German marks was equal in value to 360 or 400 Croatian dinars.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, excuse me. Can we know why this is significant? There is no doubt that in this table there are both Croatian dinars and German marks included. So we would be interested in finding out why the Prosecutor is putting this question and why the value of a German mark is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, we have to complete the examination very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The only comment, Your Honour, and I -- it can be established other ways, what the exchange rate was at the time. But just so the Chamber was not perhaps misled as to the actual size of some of these numbers. 350.000 might look like a big number, but in fact, in terms of Deutschmarks or dollars, it's not a very large number. But we'll establish that separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't want to take away the Prosecutor's time - that's not my intention - but if we want to establish the exchange rates, then that's not a problem. In this particular case, it would be 22 German marks. So what it says here is correct. But we then have to go into the cost of living in Croatia. For example, I remember that some 70 per cent of the population in Croatia in the 1990s had an income of 200 German marks a month. So this is opening Pandora's box. If we have to present evidence about this, we will. But as my colleague said, the purpose of this document is not to show the size of these amounts.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As the Prosecutor has not the said why this document is important, could we please look at page 4, that's 0328-4604, where the sum of only 20 of these entries is 418.600 German marks and 250 US dollars, and I'm leaving aside the Croatian dinars. I simply ask the witness to confirm these names, but this will lead us too far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, we really have to stop. We have to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour, but if I could have one minute, because of the interruptions in the last -- I've said very clearly what -- the relevance of why I asked: For the Chamber's information. It was a Defence exhibit, not a Prosecution exhibit, and I think it's only fair that the Chamber have some point of reference as to what the numbers are. That's my only point at this particular time. My last question to the witness is:

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, looking at the same document, do you have any personal knowledge about any of the expenditures on that page?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam, once again, I thank you for coming to The Hague, and I wish you a safe return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Now, we have to conclude because there is a hearing. Fifteen seconds for Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The monthly inflation was over 30 per cent. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Witness, on behalf of my colleagues, I would like to thank you for having come here to testify for the Prosecution. I wish you a safe trip home, and I wish you well in your consulting business. We will meet again next week at -- next week on Monday, 2.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 25th day of June, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
